Maintenance Report — MNT-0166-005

Asset: WELL-0166 (NE-08 Well 166, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 08 Jul 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 28 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0166-0037 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 09 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0166-0037 at 10:00 on 2023-07-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 0.8% of the pad area, estimated 0.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 205 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 164 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0166-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.74% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Asset: WELL-0166 (NE-08 Well 166, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 23 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 24 Feb 2024 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 29 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0166-0070 on 2024-02-22 Report written: 25 Feb 2024

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0166-0070 at 15:45 on 2024-02-22 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.0% of the pad area, estimated 4.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0166-015

Asset: WELL-0166 (NE-08 Well 166, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 19 Nov 2024 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 50 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0166-0106 on 2024-11-14 Report written: 21 Nov 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0166-0106 showed the wellhead at 16.6 °C with the air at 13.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Total13,866

Compliance check

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.
